Technology stocks turned slightly higher near Friday's close, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 were adding less than 0.1% in value while the Index still was dropping nearly 1.1%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(-) Dell Technologies ( DVMT ) was slipping almost 1% lower late Friday after S&P Global Ratings Thursday night cut its outlook for the information technology company's credit rating to negative while affirming its current ratings. A negative outlook means that a rating might be downgraded.
In other sector news:
(+) Sonos ( SONO ) spiked over 25% soon after Friday's opening bell, more recently trading just almost 11% higher after the consumer electronics company handily exceeded analyst projections withits fiscal Q4 financial results. Net loss for the company was $0.02 per share during the three months ended Sept. 30, improving on a $0.26 per share loss during the same quarter last year and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.08 per share. Revenue grew 27% year over year to a best-ever $272.9 million, also topping the Street view by around $24.06 million
(+) BlackBerry (BB,BB.TO) was more than 2% higher after the Canadian technology firm Friday moved further from its roots as a smartphone manufacturer by making its largest acquisition ever, offering to pay $1.4 billion in cash for a privately held artificial intelligence and cybersecurity specialist firm. Blackberry said its purchase of Cylance will "immediately complement" its existing portfolio and will bolster the expansion of the company's QNX unit that is developing software for next-generation autonomous cars. It also sees the deal helping its Unified Endpoint Manager business that allows clients to securely manage their device and applications fleets.
(-) NVIDIA ( NVDA ) dropped to a 15-month low on Friday, falling over 20% to its lowest share price since mid-August 2017 at $161.61 a share, after the specialty chipmaker reported non-GAAP Q3 earnings of $1.84 per share, rising 38% over the year-ago period but still lagging the Capital IQ consensus expecting $1.92 per share. Revenue increased 21% year over year to $3.18 billion but also missing the $3.24 billion analyst mean.
